"2.

This writ petition has been filed seeking quashing of the First Information Report dated 08.10.2023 in Case Crime No. 0068 of 2023, under Sections 498-A, 323, 504,
506, 354A, 34 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, Police Station- Mahila Thana, District Hapur.
"3. Counsel for the parties agree that there are chances of reconciliation between the parties and the matter should be referred to the Mediation Centre.

4. In view of the submissions made and on the petitioners depositing a sum of Rs.
30,000/- through bank draft drawn in favour of the RG A/c AHCMCC within a period of 10 days from today, the Mediation Centre shall send notice to the respondent no. 4 fixing a date for mediation.
It is also observed that attempt shall be made to conclude mediation expeditiously preferably within a period of three months.

5. List this case before appropriate Bench after three months.
6.
Till then, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners.
7. In case the amount is not deposited within the time specified above, the matter shall immediately be sent back to this Court.

8. From the amount of Rs. 30,000/- deposited, a sum of Rs. 5,000/- may be accumulated by the Mediation Centre for whatever purpose and remaining amount of Rs. 25,000/- shall be handed over to the opposite party no. 3 on the conclusion of the mediation proceedings."

4. The Registrar (Mediation)/Incharge, AHCMCC has submitted a report on 21.12.2023 indicating therein that in compliance of the order of this Court dated 06.11.2023, the petitioners were required to deposit a sum of Rs.30,000/- with the Mediation Centre of this Court but they have not deposited the amount of Rs.30,000/- at the Mediation Centre till date.
5. Considering the facts and circumstances, we are not inclined to keep the matter pending consideration.

6. However, as all alleged offences are punishable with imprisonment of seven years, therefore, the investigating agencies and their officers are duty bound to comply with the mandate of Section 41 and 41A of the Code and the directions issued in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
6. However, as all alleged offences are punishable with imprisonment of seven years, therefore, the investigating agencies and their officers are duty bound to comply with the mandate of Section 41 and 41A of the Code and the directions issued in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273.
Any dereliction on their part has to be brought to the notice of the higher authorities by the court followed by appropriate action.
The principle that bail is the rule and jail is the exception has been well recognised through the repetitive pronouncements of the Apex Court, which is on the touchstone of Article 21 of the Constitution of India (Ref. Nikesh Tarachand Shah v. Union of India,
(2018) 11 SCC 1.
This provision mandates the police officer to record his reasons in writing while making the arrest.
Thus, a police officer is duty-bound to record the reasons for arrest in writing.
The consequence of non-compliance with Section 41 shall certainly inure to the benefit of the person suspected of the offence.
On the scope and objective of Section 41 and 41A, it is obvious that they are facets of Article 21 of the Constitution.
